claims.text: adapter is the seat ask was bound from, when there was one. It is carried for ONE reason: live_egress_lanes has to hand something to session.live_egress_seats, and a bare closure is not classifiable.
claims.why: References functions live_egress_lanes and session.live_egress_seats not in this chunk.

claims.text: Nothing in the runner reads it -- the canary still calls ask and only ask, so a fake lane stays a fake lane.

claims.text: resolve_exe: Preferring the native .exe also skips the .cmd layer entirely -- the layer that truncated a multi-line argv and started all of this.
claims.why: The claim about a .cmd layer truncating argv is a historical context not verifiable from code.

claims.text: (The prompt still goes on stdin regardless; the arrival probe is what proves that end to end rather than asserting it.)

claims.text: Returns name unchanged when nothing is found, so the spawn fails as not_on_path -> unavailable instead of guessing.
